name: Confucianism
summary: Confucianism holds that social and political order springs from moral self-cultivation, with a virtuous ruler leading by example and educated, merit-selected officials assisting him. It places the family and filial piety at the root of virtue, treats society as a set of reciprocal role-based duties (ruler-subject, parent-child, husband-wife, elder-younger, friend-friend), and prefers ritual and moral transformation to law and punishment. Rulers hold Heaven's mandate only while they secure the people's welfare, and later Confucians accepted removing tyrants.
scope: The mainstream classical tradition as set out in the Analects of Confucius, developed by Mencius and Xunzi, and as carried through imperial-era orthodoxy and, where noted, modern political Confucians (meritocrats such as Jiang Qing and Daniel Bell). Many statements are modern issues the tradition never addressed, so those are low-confidence inferences from its principles. It excludes Neo-Confucian metaphysics except where it affects politics.

keyFigures.name: Confucius
keyFigures.role: Founder of the tradition and teacher whose sayings form the Analects.

keyFigures.name: Mencius
keyFigures.role: Major early successor who developed the doctrines of benevolent government and the people's welfare.

keyFigures.name: Xunzi
keyFigures.role: Early Confucian who stressed ritual, education and hierarchy as the discipline of human nature.

sources.title: The Analects (Legge translation)
sources.author: Confucius, trans. James Legge
sources.usedFor: Rule by virtue versus punishment (II.3), the ranking of food, arms and trust in government (XII.7), rectified roles (XII.11), filial piety.

sources.title: Confucius
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Rule by example, Mandate of Heaven, ritual hierarchy, family versus state, filial piety as root of loyalty.

sources.title: Mencius
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: People's livelihood, well-field system, taxation, rejection of conquest, division of labor, benevolence over profit.

sources.title: Xunzi
sources.author: Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Ritual, hierarchy, limited use of punishment, education, aggressive war as self-defeating.

sources.title: Confucianism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Five Bonds, gender norms, political meritocracy and civil service exams, right of revolution, modern debates on democracy.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Mencius wants rulers to secure the people's food, shelter and protection as a base for moral life, so state care for basic welfare is implied, but healthcare itself is never addressed.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Classical Confucianism urges a livelihood sufficient for the people but has no view on wage-setting; adherents are split on modern labor regulation.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Mencius has the state manage land and livelihood and Confucians subordinate profit to righteousness, though later thinkers praised commerce and thrift; a lean against laissez-faire inferred.

public-ownership.rationale: The well-field system gave the state a common plot but the tradition never discussed nationalizing industry; modern adherents differ.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Both Mencius and Xunzi condemn excessive taxation of the people, yet no doctrine of progressive taxation exists; inferred as undecided.

unions-good.rationale: Autonomous worker associations against employers have no place in the texts, which favor harmony through roles; the issue is anachronistic.

property-fundamental.rationale: Mencius assumes families hold land but the ruler may allocate and tax it and rights language is absent, so property is not treated as fundamental or near-inviolable.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Confucian ethics asks merchants to act with righteousness, but the texts do not address corporations and adherents differ on regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Mencius insists the ruler secure the people's livelihood and care for the helpless, so cutting welfare as harmful dependency contradicts the benevolent-government ideal.

worker-ownership.rationale: Nothing in the tradition supports collective workplace ownership; its occupational and role hierarchy points against it.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Confucius prefers moral example over coercion, but state security is not discussed and modern adherents split on surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Cultivation of self-restraint through ritual is central, so recreational drug use is disfavored, though law-based prohibition is not a classical theme.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The rectification of names and ritual speech matter, but there is no tradition on legal speech limits; inferred as split.

strong-leader.rationale: A virtuous ruler leads by example and is respected, but Confucians also hold rulers accountable to Heaven and the people's welfare, and distrust bypassing proper institutions and ritual.

state-harmful.rationale: Confucians see government by virtuous rulers as essential to moral order; the idea that the state is unnecessary is the Daoist or anarchist counterposition.

limit-guns.rationale: Confucianism favors order, rites and rare use of coercion, so strict limits fit, but the issue was never addressed.

empower-police-military.rationale: Confucius ranks arms below food and popular trust, and Xunzi says the true king wins without battle, so adherents do not stress expanding force.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Ritual propriety and family-centered sexual ethics disfavor it, though classical texts say little on legal regulation.

decide-locally.rationale: The ideal is a unified hierarchy under a virtuous sovereign, while family and local moral cultivation are the root; no clear stance on decentralization.

rehabilitation.rationale: Confucius wants moral transformation rather than mere punishment, and Xunzi holds everyone can be reformed through education, so reform of offenders fits the core view.

traditional-family.rationale: Filial piety is the root of virtue and loyalty, and the family with its roles is the basic unit of the social and political order.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Lineage continuity and male-female roles anchor Confucian marriage; modern adherents vary but the traditional stance is against.

abortion-legal.rationale: Continuation of the family line and the value placed on life and filial duty tell against it, though the classics do not address abortion.

more-religion-public.rationale: Confucianism centers ritual, Heaven and ancestor rites in public order but is not a church; some modern figures propose a state Confucian religion and others reject it.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The tradition has no analog; its concern for rectifying wrongs and helping the people does not map to racial redress.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Xunzi and the Confucian tradition treat sex roles as part of a natural and ritual order, so a view that gender is chiefly constructed is not typical.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Confucius honored the ritual and learning of the Zhou past, and Confucianism is centrally a project of transmitting and preserving cultural tradition.

gradual-change.rationale: Confucius transmitted rather than invented and worked through established rites and offices, though reformers like Kang Youwei pressed change, so the lean is moderate.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Confucius is concerned with attracting people by good rule, not restricting entry, and the issue is anachronistic.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Classical thought pictures all under Heaven ordered by virtue, but modern international organizations are not addressed.

free-trade.rationale: Classical texts favored agriculture and ranked merchants low yet later Confucians were not hostile to trade; inferred split.

nation-first.rationale: Confucius and Xunzi prize winning others by virtue over aggressive self-interest, while loyalty to one's own state and culture is assumed; split.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Mencius endorsed a benevolent state punishing a tyrant who oppresses his people, but also condemned conquest, so adherents divide.

open-borders.rationale: The ordered, role-based community of the tradition is not borderless, though the ideal of all under Heaven attracts distant peoples to virtue.

limit-growth.rationale: Confucian teaching favors thrift and restraint of desire but not capping production, and the people's livelihood is a priority.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Harmony with Heaven and nature is a theme but the tradition did not address climate policy.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Confucians locate social problems in moral cultivation and ritual rather than technique, so technology-as-solution is doubted.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No relevant teaching exists and adherents have no common view.

revolution-justified.rationale: Mencius allowed removing an evil ruler who loses Heaven's mandate and the tradition recognized a right of revolution against tyranny, though reluctantly.

experts-over-public.rationale: Confucianism entrusts government to educated, morally cultivated officials chosen by merit, and modern Confucians defend political meritocracy.

central-planning.rationale: The state shaped land allocation under the well-field idea but Confucians did not endorse comprehensive planning; the idea is anachronistic.

socialized-markets.rationale: The tradition has no view on ownership forms beyond sufficiency for the people; split.

land-value-tax.rationale: The well-field system is an early land-linked tax scheme but the single-tax idea is not Confucian doctrine.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Family continuity and passing the lineage's property and ritual duties to descendants are central, so taxing inheritance heavily conflicts with the family ethic.

basic-income.rationale: Mencius wants guaranteed livelihood but tied to work and land; unconditional income is outside the tradition.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Neither the classics nor later commentary take a position on tariffs, and adherents divide on trade protection, so neutral is inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Confucian rulers were expected to manage the people's livelihood but guided investment is a modern concern; split.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The well-field ideal gave each family its own plot, and Mencius argued a stable livelihood for ordinary families is the basis of order.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Confucian society assumes occupations, trade and a market economy within a hierarchy, and ideals of abolishing wages are alien to it.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The tradition never discusses money-issuing institutions; neutral is inferred from silence, and its respect for state management of livelihood gives no lean.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Harmony among differentiated roles resembles corporatist ideas, but state-recognized wage-setting bodies are not a Confucian doctrine.

one-party-rule.rationale: Confucian government is by virtuous rulers and scholar-officials, not a party; modern political meritocrats such as Jiang Qing propose non-party institutions.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Rule by a virtuous king holding Heaven's mandate was the Confucian ideal and imperial China was governed under Confucian principles, though legitimacy depends on virtue.

democracy-best.rationale: Classical Confucianism does not center popular rule, and leading modern defenders propose meritocracy as an alternative, though others such as Joseph Chan argue for democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Confucians trust educated, virtuous officials over mass decision-making, and even democratic Confucians favor representation.

workers-councils.rationale: Political power by workers' councils contradicts a hierarchy led by cultivated rulers.

right-to-secede.rationale: Unity under one sovereign, as a world of all under Heaven, is the ideal, so adherents resist secession, though the texts do not take it up.

natural-rulers.rationale: The junzi, the morally cultivated person, is fit to rule and the petty person is not, which is central to Confucian political thought.

political-violence-never.rationale: Confucians prefer moral example, yet Mencius allowed killing a tyrant and the tradition recognized rebellion against oppressive rule.

war-builds-character.rationale: Confucius ranks arms lowest among the needs of government and Xunzi says the aggressive state is doomed, so war as character-building is not Confucian.

separate-church-state.rationale: Ritual, Heaven and ancestor worship are woven into the government, so a strict separation is foreign, even though Confucianism is not a church.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Confucius prefers rites and virtue to law, yet the classics are the moral basis of governance; no scripture-based legal code is claimed.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Confucian government is a moral and public office held by the virtuous, so privatizing core state functions conflicts with it.

military-superiority.rationale: Arms rank below trust and food for Confucius, but states were expected to defend themselves.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Confucian standard is cultural, so Chinese civilization is defined by ritual and virtue and not ancestry, and outsiders can be transformed.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Confucianism aims at harmony among differentiated roles and criticizes the discord that class struggle presumes.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Xunzi and Confucius take unequal status and reward by role and merit as proper, though Confucius also warned against poverty and uneven distribution.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Classical Confucianism has no doctrine on indigenous peoples or land authority; neutral inferred from silence.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Reparations between states for colonialism are a modern issue absent from the texts, so neutral is inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: The all-under-Heaven ideal looks to a civilized order but no program of union by shared civilization is prescribed.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Mencius opens by rejecting profit for benevolence and righteousness, and the petty person is defined by self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Confucian ethics is built on role-based duties such as filial piety and loyalty, with rights language lacking.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Harmony with Heaven and nature is valued but the tradition is human-centered; no common view.

limit-population.rationale: Continuation of the lineage was a duty and no policy is taught.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Confucians credit work ethic with economic development and do not condemn industry, though they stress moral limits.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Confucianism values continuity of ritual and institutions over disruptive change.

human-enhancement.rationale: Self-cultivation by learning and ritual is the Confucian path, not technological modification.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Government is moral leadership by cultivated persons, so handing decisions to algorithms conflicts, though modern meritocrats might use them as tools.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption is an anachronistic issue with no Confucian teaching, so neutral is inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Confucius looked to the early Zhou as the model and saw himself as a transmitter, though the aim is moral renewal and not mere return.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Government is guided by the Way and ritual morality, not by outcomes alone.

direct-action.rationale: Change comes by ruler's example, education and remonstrance through proper channels, with revolt only as a last resort.

means-match-ends.rationale: The ruler's personal virtue is the means by which society is transformed, which makes method and aim continuous.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Confucianism is a civilization of ritual, learning and agriculture, and no source would favor foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Mencius defends specialization and says rulers govern while others farm to support them.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Mencius wants everyone's basic needs met by good rule but distribution also follows role and rank.

production-for-use.rationale: Livelihood of the people is a priority but a theory of production for use is absent.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The tradition does not treat profit as exploitation; it asks the merchant to be righteous within a cooperative occupational order.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Class dictatorship contradicts government by virtue and harmony among classes.

collective-farming.rationale: The well-field system rested on family plots, and collective farming in modern China was imposed against family-based values.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The tradition does not use this analysis and credits Confucian ethics with enabling capitalist growth in East Asia.

taxation-theft.rationale: Mencius expects rulers to tax the people lightly but legitimately; he criticizes excessive taxation and does not treat taxation as theft.

harm-principle.rationale: Confucian government may shape conduct through ritual and moral example beyond preventing harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Duties and relationship roles in family and community take priority over individual rights as the basis of ethics.

conscription.rationale: Confucius allowed military levies but ranked arms low; no stance on conscription as such.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Confucius did leave bad states and Mencius saw people flee a tyrant, but remonstrance and loyalty to the community matter more.

state-as-business.rationale: Mencius opens with a rejection of profit as the ruler's aim and expects government to be benevolent, not commercial.

positive-liberty.rationale: Mencius holds that material security enables moral life, but liberty is not the frame.

media-academia-power.rationale: Scholars were central to government in the Confucian order but the claim is a modern one.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Xunzi holds that people share a nature and differ by cultivation, and the tradition makes moral and ritual cultivation the source of difference.

organic-representation.rationale: Families and communities are the base of the social order, which is compatible with representation through them but no such system is prescribed.

total-state.rationale: Confucius opposed ruling by laws and punishments and favored family and ritual as an order beyond the state, though the ruler shapes moral culture.

national-rebirth.rationale: Confucian revivalists call for moral renewal, but the radical rebirth theme belongs to other movements.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Mencius condemns conquest by force and Xunzi says military expansion dooms the ruler.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Loyalty between ruler and minister and the five bonds matter, but Confucian authority rests on virtue and office and not feudal oaths alone.

bound-labor.rationale: Mencius supports ordered land tenure with duties, but binding farmers to land under a lord is not a Confucian principle.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Confucians hold that the Way can be known by learning and cultivation, which implies a standard beyond power.

universal-morality.rationale: Mencius holds an innate moral nature shared by all and the Way is meant for all under Heaven, though the stress is on moral cultivation not reason alone.

single-common-good.rationale: Government aims at harmony and the people's welfare under a shared Way and not at balancing opposed interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The Land of Israel and Jewish statehood lie outside the Confucian texts, so neutral is inferred.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return rights are not part of the Confucian texts; neutral is inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is not addressed by the classics; neutral inferred from silence.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Firms as role hierarchies under a virtuous head fit better than democratic voting, but the question was not addressed.

school-vouchers.rationale: Confucians prize education and private teaching, but voucher policy is unaddressed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Xunzi and Mencius warn against excessive taxation and extravagance, and thrift is a Confucian virtue, but fiscal policy is not addressed.

economic-freedom.rationale: Not discussed in the tradition; adherents differ.

rule-by-example.rationale: Confucius says rule by virtue and ritual makes people good while rule by laws and punishment only makes them avoid punishment.

national-self-determination.rationale: The tradition has no theory of nations; not addressed.

force-without-un.rationale: The UN Security Council is a modern institution unknown to the texts; neutral is inferred, with Confucian reluctance about war giving no clear lean.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Confucianism combines learning with ritual, reverence for Heaven and feeling, not reason alone.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The ruler cares for the people of his realm, but the tradition did not address immigrants; split.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Mencius connects security of livelihood to labor by families, and work is a virtue, though the helpless are to be cared for.

class-collaboration.rationale: Harmony among differently placed groups with reciprocal duties is a central aim.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Preserving classical texts and ritual heritage is the Confucian vocation, so sacrificing it for new creation is against the tradition.

dominated-front.rationale: Confucians have no common view on anti-Western fronts.

workers-nation.rationale: Whether workers organize nationally or internationally is a Marxist-era question the Confucian texts never raise.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Confucian norms assign distinct roles to men and women in family and society, though modern adherents debate it.

ban-interest.rationale: The texts do not prohibit interest, and later Confucians were not opposed to lending.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Confucian distinction is by cultivation, not race, and transformation of outsiders by virtue is expected.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Confucians see the state as moral leadership for all, not a tool of one class.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is anachronistic for the tradition, so neutral is inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The tradition expects outsiders to be transformed by Chinese ritual and culture, which is a cultural assimilation model.

elite-replacement.rationale: The conspiracy is foreign to the tradition, which treats outsiders as civilizable.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not addressed; modern Confucian debates are about meritocracy versus democracy more broadly.

national-mission.rationale: The ruler is meant to transform others by virtue and not force, but a mission to spread a form of government is not stated.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Adherents see differentiated roles as proper order, not as a system of male advantage, though critics and some feminist Confucians dispute this.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Confucians constantly criticize petty officials and urge the elite to be moral, but they defend elite rule as such.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: The tradition values family continuity and does not teach eugenics.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; accountability of rulers is moral and Heavenly.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Mencius expects government to secure the people's livelihood and moral education, far beyond a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The tradition is not racial, and this is not a Confucian concern.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Mencius holds all have the sprouts of virtue, but social roles and unequal status are affirmed and rights before the law are not a Confucian principle.

socialism-one-country.rationale: This is an internal Marxist debate on which Confucian sources say nothing; a mild no is inferred from the rejection of class revolution.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Settler colonialism as a category is modern and absent from the classics; neutral is inferred.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition preferred ritual to uniform law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Confucianism has no conversion focus and is not exclusive, though not an advocate of restriction.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Confucian tradition has no prohibition on killing cattle and its rituals include animal sacrifice, so a mild disagreement is inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Moral education in the classics is central to schooling, so a strict exclusion of moral or ritual instruction goes against the tradition.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: This is a Marxist-Leninist doctrine on which Confucian sources are silent; mild disagreement inferred from Confucian preference for virtue over coercive state power.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Heaven's mandate shows in the people's welfare and acceptance, and Mencius linked it to the people's will, but consent is not formal or electoral.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist trade balance goals are not found in the classics; neutral is inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: A benevolent ruler wins the people by virtue, and Mencius condemns harming civilians.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Confucians see harmony and cultivation as the engine of order and Xunzi uses ritual to prevent competition over scarce goods.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Party politics did not exist in the classical tradition, so neutral is inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not a Confucian concept; the tradition constrains rulers by virtue and not by a status of independence.

separated-powers.rationale: The tradition relied on a virtuous ruler with remonstrating officials, with no formal separation, though some Confucians such as Huang Zongxi limited autocracy.

vanguard-party.rationale: Leadership is by virtuous scholar-officials, not a revolutionary party.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Mencius urges rulers to care first for the helpless such as widows, orphans and the old, and Confucius warned against poverty.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Public housing sales are a modern British policy outside the texts; neutral is inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Confucianism values social harmony and lawful remonstrance, so it leans against disruptive collective action.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Mencius locates poverty in rulers' policies on land and taxes more than population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Confucianism stresses cultural unity but of ritual and not ancestry; no stance on diversity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Selection of officials by merit, learning and virtue is a core principle, the opposite of chance.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Legal protections against the state are not a classical Confucian category, so neutral is inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Confucian government is expected to guarantee the people's food, so price measures in scarcity fit.

party-controls-media.rationale: The ruler is expected to rule by example, not control information, though censorship under Confucian regimes occurred.

party-commands-army.rationale: Government by scholar-officials and a sovereign leaves no room for a ruling party commanding the army, so disagreement is inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Not a Confucian structure, which values remonstrance of superiors when they err.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization rules are not discussed in the classics; neutral inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed; Confucian officials are paid by rank.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Supranational unions are anachronistic for the texts; neutral is inferred.

head-commands-forces.rationale: In the traditional order the sovereign commands military and appoints ministers.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Confucianism has no bishops or national church hierarchy, so the issue does not apply and neutral is given.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule is by scholar-officials trained in the classics, not clergy; scholars rule as moral exemplars, which is only partly analogous.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Loyalty to one's ruler and state is assumed and Confucians would not wish its defeat.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Confucius judged music and poetry by their moral effect and the tradition shaped culture accordingly.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed; rule by a virtuous ruler holds no term limits in the classical order.

recall-officials.rationale: Mencius would remove a failing ruler, but a voter recall is a modern mechanism.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliance policy is not addressed beyond general advice to win others by virtue, so neutral is inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: The tradition accepts landlords, tenants and market exchange and has no such program.

people-in-arms.rationale: Confucius favored a trained, governed military and not an armed populace.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Agriculture was the valued basis of livelihood and Mencius's ideal rested on farming families, though Confucians also valued cities and courts.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Unity under one order is a Confucian ideal, though not a doctrine on a specific border.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Confucianism honors education as the route to virtue and rule.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The Confucian view distinguishes civilization by ritual and learning and expects others to be transformed by it.

death-penalty.rationale: Confucius favored reliance on virtue over punishment, yet Xunzi and imperial practice accepted capital punishment for grave crimes.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Confucian moral education stresses ritual and sexual propriety with gender distinction.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Evolution and creation teaching is a modern dispute not addressed by Confucian sources.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Propriety and moral cultivation favor restriction, and Confucius shaped the arts morally.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not addressed; kinship matters but the cultural frame is not blood.

minority-language-support.rationale: Minority language policy is not addressed in the classics; neutral inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions from general law for religious practice are not a Confucian concept; neutral inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Conformity to ritual and custom is how the Confucian cultivates character, so celebrating eccentricity is opposed.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International debt is a modern issue absent from the texts, so neutral is inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anti-colonial economics is not part of the classical tradition; neutral inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not addressed; modern Confucians debate democratic reform.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Asian-values discussions link Confucian cultural traits to growth, yet adherents divide on trading off freedoms.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Benevolence extended outward is a theme but no program of foreign aid is taught.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear policy is anachronistic for the texts; neutral is inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Confucian ideal selects the most virtuous, not the most popular; some modern Confucians propose elections.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banking is anachronistic for the tradition, so neutral is inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Specific territorial bargains are not addressed in the classics; neutral inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Mencius grounds livelihood and land policy in the people's welfare and rulers must ensure property supports it.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The character of the Soviet economy is a Marxist debate on which Confucian sources are silent.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Regulatory precaution on environmental risk is a modern principle not addressed by the tradition, so neutral is inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: Treaty alliances with mutual defense are not discussed in the classics; neutral inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Mencius condemned conquest and said annexing Yan needs the people's consent, but no doctrine of occupation law is stated.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Imperial Confucian states regulated religious institutions, but no common doctrine.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The sovereign's role is moral exemplar for all, above factional interests; the junzi is non-partisan.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The texts do not address secession; the unity ideal and the reluctance about war pull in opposite directions, so neutral is inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Special autonomous arrangements within a state are not addressed by the classics, so neutral is inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The ruler is the Son of Heaven with Heaven's mandate, but he is not divine and loses the mandate when wicked.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed; Mencius's tax schemes were land-based.

character-from-environment.rationale: Mencius holds an innate good nature and Xunzi holds nature is bad and must be reshaped by ritual, while both stress upbringing; the tradition is split.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The ruler is bound by virtue and Heaven's mandate, though the classical texts do not frame this as law.

space-expansion.rationale: Space expansion is anachronistic and has no Confucian teaching.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Not a classical Confucian theme; modern meritocrats propose mixed bicameral systems.

leader-cult.rationale: Honors for ritual and virtue are Confucian, but cult of personality is not, and Confucius warned against flattery.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is a modern topic not addressed by classical Confucian sources.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: This is an internal Maoist debate; Confucian sources reject class struggle as a frame, so a mild disagreement is inferred.

land-redistribution.rationale: Mencius's well-field system envisaged equal family plots and criticized land concentration.

refugee-return.rationale: Return rights of refugees are not in the classics; neutral inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The Confucian standard is cultural order and virtue, not ethnic claims.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Confucianism does not police belief; it is not a creedal faith.

women-must-cover.rationale: Classical Confucian texts do not prescribe dress rules for women in law, so neutral is inferred, though later chastity norms were strict.

common-currency.rationale: Currency unions are not addressed by the tradition; neutral is inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-ethnic or linguistic union is not a Confucian program; neutral inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority autonomy of this kind is not treated in the classics; neutral inferred.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Minority strategy of fighting for rights versus emigrating is not addressed by Confucian sources.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Mencius says livelihood enables morality but Confucians hold that ruler virtue and moral teaching drive order.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust policy is anachronistic for the tradition, so neutral is inferred.

no-bailouts.rationale: Financial bailouts are anachronistic; the tradition gives no lean, so neutral is inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Confucian rule is not by majority, and the ruler is bound by virtue.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Distinct gender roles under the traditional order tell against quotas, though some modern adherents differ.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic imperial blocs are outside the texts; neutral inferred, although agrarian self-sufficiency was valued in antiquity.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding standards in trade treaties are not addressed in the classics; neutral inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Confucius and Mencius put righteousness over profit and want officials moved by duty, though livelihood must be secured.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Mencius's rebellion requires the loss of Heaven's mandate shown by the people's welfare, not small armed groups.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The tradition honors rank and hereditary monarchy while favoring merit in office; abolition runs against the family-based order.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Confucian education centers on the classics and history of one's own civilization.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Confucians held that civilized states may transform others by virtuous example, but not necessarily rule them.

patriotic-education.rationale: Moral formation in loyalty to the community and polity is a core of Confucian schooling.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Affirmative action is a modern dispute not addressed by Confucian sources.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary design is not discussed in the classics, so neutral is inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Not addressed; Confucian ethics is credited with adapting to capitalism.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Cultivating influence in former imperial lands is not a Confucian doctrine, though Chinese tributary traditions existed; neutral inferred.

delink-world-market.rationale: Confucian societies integrated into global trade and there is no doctrine of delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The theory of a privileged working class in rich countries is Marxist and has no Confucian counterpart.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Confucian ethics is role-based and expects virtue and fairness; unrestricted private choice is not the main concern, and no stance on law.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Rights are not the foundation, and the order rests on duties and virtue; some modern Confucians accept rights as a protective tool.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The validity of colonial treaties is a modern question absent from the classics; neutral inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: The ideal ruler is the most virtuous, and in practice hereditary monarchy, though Shun's merit-based succession is idealized and modern Confucians debate elections.

minority-veto.rationale: Harmony under rulers is the aim and Confucianism does not give individuals veto over collective decisions.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Mencius held a ruler who forfeits virtue may be removed, and the tradition recognized a right of revolution against tyranny.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Not a Confucian structure, though modern Confucian democrats accept legislatures.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Mencius's ox-sparing example shows compassion for animals as a root of benevolence, though animals rank below humans.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Mencius accepts eating meat and sacrifice while urging compassion, as in the ox story.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Superiors owe benevolence to inferiors and rulers must care for the helpless, a reciprocal-duty ethic at the core of the tradition.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Confucius sought office and held that the cultivated person serves, though he accepted withdrawal under bad government.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: This is a Frankfurt School critique with no Confucian analog, though Confucius did hold that music and culture shape character; neutral is inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The Confucian account of rule is moral example and the people's trust; an analysis of hegemony is not offered.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is a modern economic analysis absent from the tradition, so neutral is inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Not addressed; Confucius valued merit and sought talent across states.

party-own-road.rationale: This concerns relations among communist parties and is not applicable to Confucian sources; neutral inferred.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy is outside the classical texts; neutral inferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Revanchist territorial claims are not addressed in the classics; neutral inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Indigenous leadership over settler descendants is a modern question not addressed by the tradition.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anti-fascism as constitutional principle is outside the Confucian tradition; neutral is inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Comparison of fascism and communism is modern and not addressed by Confucian sources; neutral inferred.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: This is an American historical dispute outside the tradition, so neutral is inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Reverence for past exemplars and heritage inclines toward preservation.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Public attention to male disadvantage is a modern question the texts do not address.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence policy is modern and not addressed in classical sources, so neutral is inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Modern Confucian thinkers argue that East Asian institutions should draw on Confucian forms such as meritocracy and not copy Western democracy.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Confucius places civil virtue over arms and the military is a subordinate instrument of government.

paid-care-work.rationale: Wages for domestic work are not discussed in the tradition, though care of elders is a core duty; neutral inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Confucians prefer moral example to coercion and Mencius condemns aggressive war, but he allowed force against tyrants, so an absolute ban is not their position.

filial-duty.rationale: Filial piety is the root of virtue and, in the Analects, of loyalty to superiors, making it the defining social duty.

office-by-exam.rationale: Merit-based office led to the imperial examination system and modern Confucians defend political meritocracy.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Not addressed; Confucianism is not tied to a view on foreign takeovers.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred: the family bond is the root of order, and ritual and duty weigh against easy dissolution.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Heaven's mandate can be lost by a tyrant, but the tradition rests on virtuous rulers and merit-selected officials, not instructed delegates.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred: Confucianism places the support of elders on the family, with the ruler providing for the aged poor.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Mencius's well-field system divides land among families under a common framework, implying it is not owned outright.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred: the tradition relies on a virtuous ruler and educated officials, not legislative approval of spending.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred: roles and duties are differentiated by relationship and merit, not judged by group outcomes.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Mencius puts benevolence over profit, and the Analects praise frugality and simple living.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Xunzi holds aggressive war self-defeating and Confucians favour winning others by virtue.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred: the tradition prefers moral example to force in dealing with other rulers.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred: Mencius opens by rejecting talk of profit in favour of benevolence, so officials serving wealthy interests would be condemned.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition's concern for cultural integrity pulls one way and its universal moral outlook the other.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Filial piety and continuing the family line weigh heavily, so state support for larger families fits, though state incentives are inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed; Mencius favours land arranged for the people's livelihood but gives no view on restricting purchasers.

job-guarantee.rationale: Mencius holds the ruler responsible for giving the people a constant livelihood, without which they cannot be moral.

democratic-peace.rationale: Confucians expect peace from virtuous rulers setting an example, and modern political Confucians doubt that electoral democracy is the best system.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Obedience to parents and legitimate rulers is a core duty, though Mencius and Xunzi allow remonstrance and removal of tyrants, so the duty is qualified rather than absent.

non-intervention.rationale: Mencius justifies punitive expeditions against tyrants who oppress their people, so absolute non-intervention is not the tradition's view.

industrial-unions.rationale: Anachronistic; the tradition has no view on union structure.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred: the tradition's culturalist, morally universal outlook holds that anyone can be transformed by virtue and gives no basis for ethnic conspiracy claims.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The family is the root of virtue and marriage a core role relationship, so abolishing its public standing is contrary to the tradition.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Split: ministers are to speak frankly to the ruler and rulers answer to the people, but paternalistic rule sits uneasily with a legal right of public access.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from Mencius's agrarian vision of households farming their own land.

informal-organisation.rationale: Inferred: ritual, hierarchy and established institutions are central, so informal leaderless groups are not the model.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition's all-under-heaven outlook and modern political Confucians' views on sovereignty pull in different directions.

religious-nation.rationale: Community is defined by shared ritual, culture and moral self-cultivation rather than creed, so a religion-defined nation is not its model.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from the Sinocentric tributary order, which grew out of Confucian ideas of hierarchy and ritual; modern Confucians are split.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from Confucian stress on hierarchical unity under a virtuous ruler and a shared livelihood for all the people.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Mencius's well-field system gave families private plots beside a common one, so full common ownership of productive land is not endorsed.

defeat-communism.rationale: Not addressed; Mencius rejects conquest while modern Confucians divide over communism, so this is genuinely split.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred: Confucianism requires government to secure the people's livelihood but is indifferent to who delivers services.

religion-illusion.rationale: Confucius keeps reverence for Heaven and ritual and treats religion as a moral practice, not an illusion, while staying agnostic about spirits.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Anachronistic; Mencius ranks benevolence over profit, but modern Confucians divide over markets, so this is split.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Five Bonds and the traditional gender norms rest on role hierarchy, so equality is not framed as an economic goal.

socialized-care.rationale: Filial piety and family duty are the root of virtue, so care belongs in the family and not the state.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred: no Confucian text addresses loanwords, and the tradition's emphasis on cultural refinement gives no support for purging them.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from Analects XII.7, which ranks trust as government's most vital asset, so promises should be kept.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred from the family-and-state hierarchy under a ruler, which does not endorse small communes holding property in common.

majority-settlement.rationale: Not addressed; Confucian thought on civilising outlying peoples is contested and settlement policy is never discussed.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Anachronistic; modern political Confucians split on whether a Confucian meritocracy is a third way.

missingStatements.text: Children owe their parents lifelong respect, care and support.
missingStatements.rationale: Filial piety is the root of virtue and, in the Analects, of loyalty to superiors, making it the defining social duty.

missingStatements.text: Social order depends on each person fulfilling the duties of their role, such as ruler, parent, spouse or child.
missingStatements.rationale: The Five Bonds and the rectification of names make reciprocal role duties the core of social harmony.

missingStatements.text: Government office should go to those who show learning and moral virtue, selected by examination rather than birth.
missingStatements.rationale: Merit-based office led to the imperial examination system and modern Confucians defend political meritocracy.

notes: Strands differ: Mencius is more favorable to popular welfare and revolt, Xunzi to ritual hierarchy and punishment, and modern Confucians divide between meritocrats and democrats. Most economic and international statements are modern and answered as low-confidence inferences. Primary source is the Analects only; Mencius and Xunzi are cited through scholarly entries.
